sources.entry: restic REST Server | High-performance HTTP server backend for restic backups

summary.one_liner: rest-server is a standalone HTTP server that implements restic's REST backend API, letting restic clients back up to a remote server over HTTP or HTTPS.
summary.what_it_does: Rest Server is a Go HTTP server that implements the REST backend API used by the restic backup client, so restic can use it via a rest: URL. It stores repository data in a directory on the server using the same layout as restic's local backend, so the data can also be accessed locally. It supports HTTP or TLS (with a configurable minimum TLS version), Basic Authentication via a .htpasswd file, or disabling authentication. Additional options include append-only mode, private per-user repositories, a maximum repository size, group-accessible file permissions, and an optional Prometheus metrics endpoint. It can also trust proxy headers for client addresses and delegate authentication to a reverse proxy via a username header. The README also describes a systemd service and socket example and a Docker image with user-management commands.
use_cases: host a remote restic backup repository on my own server
run append-only backups that ransomware or attackers cannot wipe
serve restic backups to multiple users with separate repositories
back up over HTTPS through a firewall that only allows web traffic
run a backup target in a Docker container
run a backup server as a systemd service
notable: Append-only mode prevents deletion or modification of existing backups from the client side
Uses the same directory structure as restic's local backend, so data is accessible both locally and over HTTP
Optional private repositories so users cannot access each other's repos
Docker image supports running as an arbitrary user with a read-only root filesystem
Prometheus metrics endpoint with an example Grafana dashboard in examples/compose-with-grafana/
caveats: Default storage path is the OS temp directory; backups are lost if the default path is used, so --path must be set
Requires restic v0.7.1 or higher and Go 1.26 or higher to build; the official Go compiler is the only tested one
Basic authentication sends credentials in clear text without TLS, and self-signed certificates must be distributed to every client
Proxy authentication trusts the username header, so the proxy must be trusted to prevent forgery
